title: Family
description: Talk about your family and use the possessive の.

grammar_note.title: の links nouns (possession)
grammar_note.body: の works like English 's or 'of': わたしの ちち = my father, ともだちの ねこ = my friend's cat. Note the humble/honorific split: use ちち・はは for YOUR OWN father/mother, but おとうさん・おかあさん when talking about someone else's parents (or addressing your own).

culture_note: Japanese family terms change depending on whose family you mean — humble words for your own family (ちち, はは, あに), respectful words for others' (おとうさん, おかあさん, おにいさん). Mixing them up is a classic beginner mistake locals find endearing!

objectives: Distinguish humble vs honorific family terms

study_guide.heading: の links nouns
study_guide.body: の shows possession like 's: わたしの ちち = my father, ともだちの ねこ = my friend's cat.

study_guide.heading: Your family vs theirs
study_guide.body: Use ちち/はは for YOUR father/mother, but おとうさん/おかあさん for someone else's (or to address your own). It's a politeness distinction.

study_guide.heading: Counting people
study_guide.body: ひとり (1), ふたり (2), then number + にん: さんにん (3 people). かぞくは よにんです = 4 in my family.
